title: Breast cancer
summary: Breast cancer (except sarcoma - see 13.04) that is A) locally advanced, B) with extensive nodal/distant metastases, C) recurrent (except local recurrence that remits with therapy), D) small-cell (oat cell), or E) with secondary lymphedema caused by anticancer therapy treated by surgery to salvage or restore an upper extremity (presumptive 12 months from surgery).

children.criterion: Breast cancer (except sarcoma - evaluate sarcoma under 13.04). See 13.00K4.
Paragraph A, B, C, D, or E
Locally advanced cancer (inflammatory carcinoma, cancer of any size with direct extension to the chest wall or skin, or cancer of any size with metastases to the ipsilateral internal mammary nodes)
Carcinoma with metastases to the supraclavicular or infraclavicular nodes, to 10 or more axillary nodes, or with distant metastases
Recurrent carcinoma, except local recurrence that remits with anticancer therapy

With secondary lymphedema caused by anticancer therapy and treated by surgery to salvage or restore the functioning of an upper extremity (see 13.00K4b). Consider under a disability until at least 12 months from the date of the surgery that treated the secondary lymphedema. Thereafter, evaluate any residual impairment(s) under the criteria for the affected body system.
